summary_en: This phase II trial tests adding proton spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) or photon stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to pembrolizumab before surgery. It studies patients with locally advanced or locoregionally recurrent oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma who have not had prior radiation. Patients receive SFRT or SBRT every other day for up to 3 treatments over 1 week, and pembrolizumab IV on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for up to 2 cycles. Surgery is planned within 8 weeks after finishing pembrolizumab. The record does not state a main outcome; it is a phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II evalúa agregar radioterapia de fraccionamiento espacial con protones (SFRT) o radioterapia estereotáctica corporal con fotones (SBRT) a pembrolizumab antes de la cirugía. Incluye a pacientes con carcinoma de células escamosas de cavidad oral localmente avanzado o recurrente en la región, que no han recibido radioterapia previa. Los pacientes reciben SFRT o SBRT en días alternos, hasta 3 tratamientos en una semana, y pembrolizumab por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 3 semanas, hasta 2 ciclos. La cirugía está prevista dentro de las 8 semanas posteriores a terminar el pembrolizumab. El registro no indica un resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Oral cavity squamous cell cancer that is not linked to HPV or p16, and is locally advanced (T3-T4) without spread
Oral cavity cancer that has come back in the region and has not had radiation before
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower
Eligible for immunotherapy after multidisciplinary review, with PD-L1 combined positive score of 1 or more
not_for: Participation in another study with an investigational product in the last 3 months
Prior radiation therapy to the head and neck
Anticancer therapy within 30 days before registration, or without an adequate washout period
Uncontrolled medical or psychiatric conditions that limit consent or ability to take part
cancer_types: locally advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma
locally recurrent oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma
